texts.arguments: 7. The petitioner Shri Praveen Mehra appeared in the witness box as PW1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/A reiterating the averments made in the claim petition. As the petition has been filed U/s 166 M.V Act it was incumbent upon the petitioner to prove that he sustained injuries in an accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows: Praveen Mehra vs Rajeev Kapoor on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45278290/ 4 "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents/claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal (supra). On perusal Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 8 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. Proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard. Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on part of the driver." It is established law that in a claim petition under Motor Vehicle Act, the standard of proof to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle is not at par with the criminal case where such rashness and negligence is required to be proved beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt. In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 9 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. 11. He admitted that he was driving the motorcycle. He denied the suggestion that the accident had taken place due to his negligence. Thus PW1 stated that he had drunk beer prior to the accident. It was argued on behalf of the insurance company that the petitioner had consumed alcohol at the time of the accident and dashed the motorcycle against the Praveen Mehra vs Rajeev Kapoor on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45278290/ 6 alleged offending vehicle In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 13 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. the accident. The MLC of the petitioner is on record as per which the nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. Thus it stands established that the petitioner had sustained injuries in the alleged accident. The law is well settled that the compensation has to be awarded in personal injury cases under the following heads: (1) for loss of earnings during the period of treatment (2) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (3) Suit No. D 135/15 Page no. 14 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. expenses suffered by him on his treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food etc. In addition, he is further entitled to non pecuniary damages/general damages which include (1) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries and (2) loss of expectation of life. MEDICINES AND MEDICAL TREATMENT 17. The case of the petitioner is that due to the accident on 25.2.2015 he fell down on the road and received multiple grievous injuries. The petitioner was removed to RML Hospital, New Delhi where MLC was prepared by the doctors of the concerned hospital. It was submitted that due to the accident the petitioner received multiple grievous injuries and other specific injuries and wounds, swelling and pain on different parts of the body and the petitioner had spent a huge amount on his treatment but he was not well, therefore his all deposited money was spent on his treatment but he was not well, then he arranged more money from his relatives as a friendly loan which was already spent on his treatment but the same was not returned by him till date. It was stated that an amount of Rs.5,00,000/ was spent on the treatment and the treatment was still continuing. It was averred that the petitioner was not doing any work because pain and suffering was continuing in his body till date and he had spent his all money on conveyance charges, room charges, attendant charges, on medical prescriptions and on purchasing the medicines and on Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 15 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. special diet and other connected charges, etc. but he was not well till date because pain and suffering was continuing in his body till date. It was contended that due to the accident the petitioner and his family members suffered from mental pain and agony, loss of income, loss of works, loss of enjoyment, loss of social activities, loss of general or special damages, etc. The petitioner in paras 1, 2, 3 and 4 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had deposed to that effect. He stated that he received grievous injuries and pelvis fracture right side and of second metatarsal bone. 18. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and as per the same nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. Thus the petitioner had not received any disability due to the accident. It cannot be disputed that the petitioner had sustained injuries and underwent treatment for the same. The petitioner had stated that he had spent an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/ on his treatment. The petitioner had filed bills for an amount of Rs. 44,383/ approximately. Looking to the nature of the injuries the petitioner is held entitled to the amount of the bills. The petitioner would incur some expenses even subsequently. Accordingly an amount of Rs.50,000/ is awarded towards medical treatment and expenses including the amount of the bills. PAIN AND SUFFERING AND LOSS OF AMENITIES OF LIFE 19. It has been held in Divisional Controller, K. S. R. T. C v Mahadeva Shetty and another AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4172 as under: 13."The damages for vehicular accidents are in the nature of compensation in money for loss of any kind caused to any person. In case of personal injury the position is different from loss of property. In Parry V. Cleaver (1969 1 All. E. R. 555) Lord Morris stated as follows: Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 17 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. "To compensate in money for pain and for the physical consequences is invariably difficult, but...... no other process can be devised than that of making monetary assessment." It was submitted that due to the accident the petitioner received multiple grievous injuries and other specific injuries and wounds, swelling and pain on different parts of the body. It was averred that the petitioner was not doing any work because pain and suffering was continuing in his body till date and he was not well till date because pain and suffering was continuing in his body till date. The petitioner stated that he received grievous injuries and pelvis fracture right side and of second metatarsal bone. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and as per the same nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. The documents placed on record show that the petitioner had suffered fracture of pelvis right side and fracture of 2nd metatarsal base. The documents also show that he remained admitted in hospital. However there is nothing to show that the petitioner had sustained any disability in the accident. Looking at the nature of injuries and extent of treatment and that the accident pertains to the year 2015, the petitioner is awarded Rs.30,000/ (Rs.Thirty Thousand only) for pain and suffering. 20. The petitioner was 28 years of age at the time of the accident and it was so stated in the claim petition. As such he would have been more than 27 years old on the date of the accident i.e. 25.2.2015. The petitioner cannot however be held to be entitled to any amount towards loss of expectation of life or towards disfiguration. The petitioner had placed on record bills towards ambulance charges for an amount of Rs.5,800/ though one bill is not dated. 22. The petitioner in para 3 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had stated that he spent money on conveyance charges, medical prescriptions, purchasing the medicines and on special diet and other connected expenses. Although the petitioner has not proved any document to show that he was advised special diet, notice can be taken of the fact that the petitioner might have taken diet rich in protein, Praveen Mehra vs Rajeev Kapoor on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45278290/ 10 vitamins and minerals for speedier recovery. In the circumstances the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/ (Rs.Five Thousand only) for special diet. 23. The petitioner in para 4 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had stated that his elder brother had taken leave for him as attendant for the period of bed rest as he was on complete bed rest for 45 months. However nothing has been produced on record to show what the brother of the petitioner was doing or to establish that he had indeed taken leave. Although the petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that he incurred any expenses towards attendant charges, however looking to the nature of injuries the petitioner would have incurred some expenditure on attendant charges and a sum of Rs. 9,000/ is awarded towards attendant charges. LOSS OF INCOME 24. It is the case of the petitioner that at the time of accident he was 28 years old and was doing his selfbusiness of Videography and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month which was handsome income to run his family but due to the accident he was on bed rest and long treatment and he lost his income and suffered from heavy loss of income as well as expenses on treatment which were continuing till date. The petitioner in para 4 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had deposed to that effect. He stated that after the accident his work was stopped due to long time treatment and he was suffering economic problem. He stated that he was on bed rest for 45 months and he could not work properly, therefore, he was facing great financial losses and other irreparable losses. However the petitioner has not placed on record any Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 21 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. document to show what he was doing or how much amount he was earning. During cross examination by the learned counsel for the insurance company PW1 stated that he had not placed on record any proof of his income. He denied the suggestion that he was not earning Rs.20,000/ to Rs.30,000/ p.m. He stated that he had one brother. He denied the suggestion that he had not taken leave on account of his injuries. He denied the suggestion that he did not suffer any financial loss on account of the accident. Thus PW1 himself stated that he had not placed on record any proof of his income. As such there is nothing to show that the petitioner was earning Rs.20,000/ to Rs.30,000/ per month at the time of the accident. During examination by the Tribunal the petitioner stated that he was 25 years old. He stated that at the time of the accident he was working as a photographer and was earning Rs.15,000/ to Rs.20,000/ per month. 25. The petitioner had stated that he remained on bed rest for 45 months but the petitioner has not produced any document to show that he remained on bed rest for any particular period and there is nothing to show that he was advised bed rest for any particular period or that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to work or to show the period for which he was not able to work except one document advising bed rest for 10 days. There is also nothing to show that he remained on bed rest for 45 months. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.30,000/ consolidated on account of loss of Suit No. Praveen Mehra vs Rajeev Kapoor on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45278290/ 11 D135/15 Page no. 22 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. income. 26. There is also nothing to show that the petitioner had suffered any disability on account of the injuries. The petitioner has not proved that he acquired any disability on account of the accident or that he is likely to suffer future loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident and that the injuries would reduce his efficiency to work and thereby he would suffer loss of future income. Accordingly the petitioner cannot be held entitled to any amount on account of loss of future prospects.

It was contended that due to the accident the petitioner and his family members suffered from mental pain and agony, loss of income, loss of works, loss of enjoyment, loss of social activities, loss of general or special damages, etc. The petitioner in paras 1, 2, 3 and 4 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had deposed to that effect. He stated that he received grievous injuries and pelvis fracture right side and of second metatarsal bone. 18. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and as per the same nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. Thus the petitioner had not received any disability due to the accident. It cannot be disputed that the petitioner had sustained injuries and underwent treatment for the same. The petitioner had stated that he had spent an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/ on his treatment. The petitioner had filed bills for an amount of Rs. 44,383/ approximately. Looking to the nature of the injuries the petitioner is held entitled to the amount of the bills. The petitioner would incur some expenses even subsequently. Accordingly an amount of Rs.50,000/ is awarded towards medical treatment and expenses including the amount of the bills. PAIN AND SUFFERING AND LOSS OF AMENITIES OF LIFE 19. It was submitted that due to the accident the petitioner received multiple grievous injuries and other specific injuries and wounds, swelling and pain on different parts of the body. It was averred that the petitioner was not doing any work because pain and suffering was continuing in his body till date and he was not well till date because pain and suffering was continuing in his body till date. The petitioner stated that he received grievous injuries and pelvis fracture right side and of second metatarsal bone. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and as per the same nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. The documents placed on record show that the petitioner had suffered fracture of pelvis right side and fracture of 2nd metatarsal base. The documents also show that he remained admitted in hospital. However there is nothing to show that the petitioner had sustained any disability in the accident. Looking at the nature of injuries and extent of treatment and that the accident pertains to the year 2015, the petitioner is awarded Rs.30,000/ (Rs.Thirty Thousand only) for pain and suffering. 20. The petitioner was 28 years of age at the time of the accident and it was so stated in the claim petition. The petitioner had placed on record bills towards ambulance charges for an amount of Rs.5,800/ though one bill is not dated. Although the petitioner has not proved any document to show that he was advised special diet, notice can be taken of the fact that the petitioner might have taken diet rich in protein, Praveen Mehra vs Rajeev Kapoor on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45278290/ 10 vitamins and minerals for speedier recovery. In the circumstances the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/ (Rs.Five Thousand only) for special diet. 23. The petitioner in para 4 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had stated that his elder brother had taken leave for him as attendant for the period of bed rest as he was on complete bed rest for 45 months. However nothing has been produced on record to show what the brother of the petitioner was doing or to establish that he had indeed taken leave. Although the petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that he incurred any expenses towards attendant charges, however looking to the nature of injuries the petitioner would have incurred some expenditure on attendant charges and a sum of Rs. 9,000/ is awarded towards attendant charges. LOSS OF INCOME 24. It is the case of the petitioner that at the time of accident he was 28 years old and was doing his selfbusiness of Videography and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month which was handsome income to run his family but due to the accident he was on bed rest and long treatment and he lost his income and suffered from heavy loss of income as well as expenses on treatment which were continuing till date. The petitioner in para 4 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had deposed to that effect. He stated that after the accident his work was stopped due to long time treatment and he was suffering economic problem. He stated that he was on bed rest for 45 months and he could not work properly, therefore, he was facing great financial losses and other irreparable losses. However the petitioner has not placed on record any Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 21 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. document to show what he was doing or how much amount he was earning. During cross examination by the learned counsel for the insurance company PW1 stated that he had not placed on record any proof of his income. He denied the suggestion that he was not earning Rs.20,000/ to Rs.30,000/ p.m. He stated that he had one brother. He denied the suggestion that he had not taken leave on account of his injuries. He denied the suggestion that he did not suffer any financial loss on account of the accident. Thus PW1 himself stated that he had not placed on record any proof of his income. As such there is nothing to show that the petitioner was earning Rs.20,000/ to Rs.30,000/ per month at the time of the accident. During examination by the Tribunal the petitioner stated that he was 25 years old. He stated that at the time of the accident he was working as a photographer and was earning Rs.15,000/ to Rs.20,000/ per month. 25. The petitioner had stated that he remained on bed rest for 45 months but the petitioner has not produced any document to show that he remained on bed rest for any particular period and there is nothing to show that he was advised bed rest for any particular period or that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to work or to show the period for which he was not able to work except one document advising bed rest for 10 days. There is also nothing to show that he remained on bed rest for 45 months. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.30,000/ consolidated on account of loss of Suit No. Praveen Mehra vs Rajeev Kapoor on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45278290/ 11 D135/15 Page no. 22 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. income. 26. There is also nothing to show that the petitioner had suffered any disability on account of the injuries. The petitioner has not proved that he acquired any disability on account of the accident or that he is likely to suffer future loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident and that the injuries would reduce his efficiency to work and thereby he would suffer loss of future income. Accordingly the petitioner cannot be held entitled to any amount on account of loss of future prospects.
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: On perusal Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 8 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 9 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. 11. In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 13 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. the accident. The law is well settled that the compensation has to be awarded in personal injury cases under the following heads: (1) for loss of earnings during the period of treatment (2) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (3) Suit No. D 135/15 Page no. 14 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. expenses suffered by him on his treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food etc. It has been held in Divisional Controller, K. S. R. T. C v Mahadeva Shetty and another AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4172 as under: 13."The damages for vehicular accidents are in the nature of compensation in money for loss of any kind caused to any person. In case of personal injury the position is different from loss of property. In Parry V. Cleaver (1969 1 All. E. R. 555) Lord Morris stated as follows: Suit No. D135/15 Page no. 17 of 26 Praveen Mehra v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. "To compensate in money for pain and for the physical consequences is invariably difficult, but...... no other process can be devised than that of making monetary assessment."
